extracted.intended_audience: federal agency officials, administrative law scholars, practitioners, and policymakers interested in rulemaking, adjudication, and enforcement
extracted.subtask_short: agency rulemaking and adjudication best practices
extracted.subtask_description: Summarize and apply ACUS recommendations for (1) expanding nonlawyer representation in agency adjudications, (2) inviting public participation when agencies forgo notice-and-comment, and (3) safely using algorithmic/AI tools in enforcement. Intended to guide agency practice and commentary on administrative procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expanding Access to Nonlawyer Representation in Agency Adjudications
rubrics_metrics.description: ACUS recommends allowing nonlawyers to represent parties in agency adjudications; best practices for expanding access to justice by increasing the availability of nonlawyer representatives and support for participants in federal agency adjudications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopted at ACUS's December 2024 plenary; the recommendation focuses on increasing availability of nonlawyer representatives and supports to expand access to justice in agency adjudications. The Regulatory Review invited ACUS staff and scholars to reflect on the purpose and intended impact of this recommendation (essay by Lea Robbins and Amy Widman).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Engagement in Expedited Agency Rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: ACUS recommends inviting public participation in rulemaking even when agencies forgo notice and comment; best practices to help agencies maintain robust public participation when they find good cause not to use normal notice-and-comment procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framed as guidance for agencies that use 'good cause' to avoid normal notice-and-comment: the recommendation provides practices for preserving meaningful public participation in expedited or nontraditional rulemaking processes. Discussed in an essay by Mark Squillace in the Regulatory Review series.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Practices for AI and Algorithmic Tools in Regulatory Enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: ACUS offered guidance on how agencies can safely and responsibly use algorithmic tools, including artificial intelligence, in regulatory enforcement; recommended best practices for AI and algorithmic tools to detect and prosecute regulatory violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation addresses use of algorithmic systems in enforcement settings, emphasizing safety and responsibility. The Regulatory Review invited Kazia Nowacki of ACUS to discuss the perils and promise of AI in regulatory enforcement and the intended impact of these best practices.
